ref_issue.title: fix(large-node/fprime): widen the aliveNodes liveness mask to U64
ref_issue.body:
`CspBridge.cpp` builds the liveness mask as `U8 alive = 0` and tests `alive & (1U << node)`, and `CspBridge.fpp` publishes `aliveNodes` as `U8`. Only addresses 0 to 7 have a bit. #154 adds a `static_assert` over `TRACKED_NODES` so a node above 7 fails the build instead of dropping out of the mask silently, but the band allocation in `node_ids.h` starts small nodes at 8, so the mask has to grow before any tracked node uses the bands.

Scope:

- `aliveNodes` to `U64` in `CspBridge.fpp`, bit n meaning CSP address n, so ground decoding needs no table.
- The mask build and test in `CspBridge.cpp`, and the `static_assert` bound from 8 to 64.
- The CspBridge unit tests and `tests/e2e/check_protocol.py` where they decode the channel.
- Dictionary impact: the channel type changes, so fprime-gds and any Yamcs mapping pick up the new dictionary.
- `node_ids.h`: replace the "8-bit mask binds first" paragraph with the 6-bit sender field as the single limit.

Refs #120, #154. Blocks the MCU move to the small node band and the radio node.

ref_issue.title: fix(small-node): record broadcast as reserved and refuse to send it
ref_issue.body:
Refs #125. The driver follow-up stays in #125, as agreed there, so this does not close it.

The pbuf question is answered in the issue with the code: the destination is examined after allocation, not before, so a promiscuous filter holds a buffer per foreign transfer rather than costing a queue entry. Option 1 stays off the table for the EPS.

## Broadcast refusal

A Zephyr node could send to `0x3FFF`: the SBC would receive it and the other Zephyr nodes would not, because they filter on destination in hardware, so a broadcast service would look like it works while delivering to part of the bus. Every send from the small node now goes through `roci_csp_send`, which refuses a connection whose remote end is the broadcast address. It logs at error level, frees the packet, since callers hand over ownership, and never calls `csp_send`: reserved means the firmware does not emit it. One choke point instead of eight call sites, which also covers the bench KISS interface, where nothing filters.

The remote end of a connection is `csp_conn_src()`, on client and server connections alike. `csp_conn_dst()` is 0 on an outgoing connection, which is why the first version of this check never fired. The `roci_csp` ztest suite runs the real `csp_setup.c` on the native_sim CAN loopback and counts frames on the bus: one for a unicast send, none for a broadcast, with the buffer returned.

## Documentation

Heartbeat, SYNC and time distribution were all described as broadcasts, and all three are unicast in the implementation, so `csp_ports.h`, `sync.h`, `heartbeat.h`, `hk.h` and BAC-FSW-SDD-001 are corrected. The SDD now separates the two purposes of the heartbeat: node to controller, unicast and implemented, and controller to nodes, one-to-many and planned until the Zephyr nodes receive broadcast. SYNC stays per-node unicast, and the SDD bounds what that aligns: one CAN frame per trigger, about 0.26 ms of bus time at 500 kbit/s, plus the command dispatch between triggers. The port section states that broadcast is defined by CFP2, reserved, refused by the firmware and not received by Zephyr nodes. `COM-09` keeps its wording, since it is a requirement rather than a claim about the implementation.

## Cost

Flash on `eps_node.conf` is 9.54 percent against 9.53 on main, with RAM unchanged at 37.34 percent.

## Validation

Validation on ab7dae2 with the main fix from #162 merged in: the CI matrix 25 of 25, which covers every non-EPS overlay; `roci_power` 12 of 12 and `roci_csp` 2 of 2; and the e2e run, 29 of 29 over 119 frames with the deployment's clock started on 15 September (see #161).

ref_issue.title: refactor(shared): derive the rail state bits from the rail identifier
ref_issue.body:
Closes #104.

Two vocabularies describe the same rails: `enum bac_pwr_rail` in the telecommand payload, and the `BAC_PWR_ST_*` bits in the housekeeping byte. The issue asks to reconcile them, or at minimum to document the mapping. This does both.

Documenting it alone would have left the mapping exactly where it was. Both places that held the two vocabularies together did it by hand, and either could drift: `bac_power_set_rail` carried the bit inside the same switch that picks the GPIO, so adding a rail meant remembering two things in one case arm; and `handle_rail` took the rail and its enable mask as separate arguments, with the two call sites keeping them in agreement by eye.

`roci_pwr_rail_en_bit` states the mapping once, in `shared/include/bac/pwr_rails.h`, so the firmware and anything decoding the housekeeping byte reach the same answer. It lives next to `msg_defs.h` rather than in it, since the wire header is included into C++ by `CspBridge` and stays declarative. The new symbol takes the `roci_` prefix; the existing names keep theirs until the retrofit in #105.

The mapping came from the code rather than from the comments: `BAC_RAIL_5V_MAIN` is VREG_1 and `BAC_RAIL_3V3_MAIN` is VREG_2, as both `bac_power_set_rail` and `handle_rail` already had them. VBAT has no regulator enable line, so it maps to 0, and `bac_power_set_rail` still refuses it in its own enum switch before deriving the bit.

Appendix A of BAC-FSW-SDD-001 tables the full mapping, each enum value and the charger against its regulator and its enable and PGOOD bits, and R13 is marked resolved.

`bac_power_rails_up` keeps naming the bits directly. It drives an ordered power-up sequence rather than acting on a rail identifier, so routing it through the helper would add indirection without removing a mapping.

## Validation

Validation on 0ec086b with the main fix from #162 merged in: the CI matrix 25 of 25, and `roci_power` 12 of 12, the suite that asserts on the rail state byte.

ref_issue.body:
## Context

The direction in the #154 review: the SBC holds the controller role for the Dev Kit, controller is a role rather than a node, and small nodes reach it only through `CONFIG_BAC_PEER_ADDRESS`. #154 writes that into section 3.1 of BAC-FSW-SDD-001 and makes the firmware match it. The review left the systematic pass through the rest of the SDD to its own issue, which is this one. It matters beyond wording: #39 records that after Dev Kit v1 the OBC role moves off the CM5 to a medium node.

## Scope

On the #154 branch the SDD names the SBC 224 times on 179 lines. Most of those describe what the controller does: sending telecommands, distributing time and SYNC, tracking liveness, receiving housekeeping and alerts, taking over the heartbeat after boot, commanding mode transitions. Those become "controller". The ones that describe the CM5 itself, its F Prime deployment or the Dev Kit hardware stay "SBC", section 3.2 included.

The mentions concentrate in sections 3.6 and 3.7 (the interface and responsibility matrices), 5.3 to 5.5 (message categories, data flow and bus redundancy), 6.1 (telecommands), 7.1 (boot and the heartbeat handover), 8.2 (time distribution), 9.3 and 9.4 (recovery and watchdog) and the M3 milestone in 11.3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every remaining "SBC" in BAC-FSW-SDD-001 means the CM5 node or its software, not the role
- [ ] Diagrams and tables use the same term as the prose
- [ ] Revision history entry

Depends on #154.

ref_issue.title: CAN hardware validation on EPS board (T1–T5)
ref_issue.body:
## Context

Repeat the PoC validation tests (T1–T5) on the real EPS hardware to confirm CAN communication works with the TCAN334G transceivers and the EPS board layout.

## Scope

- [ ] T1: Raw CAN TX/RX — 100 frames, no CSP layer
- [ ] T2: CSP Ping — libcsp built-in service (port 1)
- [ ] T3: Heartbeat at 2 Hz — CSP port 8, sustained
- [ ] T4: Fragmented HK (64 B) — CSP fragmentation over CAN
- [ ] T5: Bus error recovery — CAN error state monitoring and FDIR
- [ ] Test both CAN1 and CAN2 independently
- [ ] Document results in updated test report (TR-001 or new TR)

## Notes

- PoC used WeAct STM32F405 + SN65HVD230 at 500 kbps — all T1–T5 PASS
- EPS uses TCAN334G transceivers with GPIO-controlled standby and shutdown:
  - **CAN1:** STB on PB4 (pull-down), SHDN on PB5 (pull-down) — **enabled by default** (low = active)
  - **CAN2:** STB on PB14 (pull-up), SHDN on PB15 (pull-up) — **in standby by default** (high = standby)
  - Firmware must drive PB14 and PB15 **low** to enable CAN2 before using the redundant bus
  - CAN1 requires no GPIO action at boot (already enabled by pull-down defaults)
- The bxCAN driver is the same — transceiver change should be transparent, but needs validation
- TCAN334G STB pin: LOW = normal operation, HIGH = standby (low-power, bus recessive)
- TCAN334G SHDN pin: LOW = normal operation, HIGH = shutdown (outputs hi-Z)

## Depends on

- #21 (EPS board definition)
- EPS boards arriving (~early May 2026)

## References

- PoC test report: `docs/BAC-FSW-TR-001.md`
- Test procedure: `docs/BAC-FSW-TP-001.md`
- TCAN334G datasheet: TI SLLSEZ5

Status update, since parts of the description above went stale.

- CAN1 does not come up on its own. PB4 leaves reset as the JTAG NJTRST pin with its internal pull-up on, which beats the board pull-down on STB, so the transceiver sat in standby. Bits 5 and 6 carry a 2-bit packet counter, so consecutive packets do not repeat an identifier; `candump can0,00030080:07FFFF80` matches every frame the EPS sends to the SBC. Until #154 lands, the old table holds.

## Context

PR #94 implements the EPS firmware end to end (power-rail control, charger +
load-switch diagnostics, NOMINAL/SAFE mode with autonomous FDIR, CAN2 failover,
RTC + time distribution, power-threshold alerts, telecommands, SYNC and PARAM).
Code-complete and builds (eps_node + eps_t4), but not yet run on hardware. This
tracks bench bring-up on the EPS Main Board v2r3 (flash via ST-Link/SWD on J801).

Pre-req: remove the inhibit jumpers (JP101 RBF / JP102 DSW) so the MCU boots.

## Scope

- [ ] Flash + boot; watchdog keeps the board alive (no resets).
- [ ] Rails: EN drive, PGOOD asserts, INA219 currents read.
- [ ] Charger STB enable/standby + STAT read.
- [ ] Safe mode: SAFE_MODE input forces SAFE (sheds 5V); EXIT_SAFE restores; held-high input does not flap (edge latch).
- [ ] Autonomous recovery: drop a rail PGOOD -> re-enable retries -> FDIR + safe mode.
- [ ] RTC: SBC sets clock (port 10), rtc_epoch tracks, survives a power cycle (LSE + backup battery).
- [ ] Power alerts on threshold (port 16).
- [ ] Telecommands (port 12) + responses; PARAM read (port 13); SYNC (port 9) -> HK snapshot.

## Related
- CAN T1-T5: #22
- CAN failover T6 + fail-back: #28
- SBC HK consumer: #95
